ETDatacenters Updated On Oct 14, 2026 at 11:30 AM IST Highlights CtrlS Datacenters will invest $1 billion to build a 150 MW AI factory in Bodh Gaya. The company signed a Letter of Intent with the Government of Bihar for the project. A new 12 MW AI and cloud-ready data center in Patna was inaugurated. CtrlS plans to expand to over 20 Edge data centers across India and 4.4 GW capacity by 2030. CtrlS Datacenters Ltd. plans to invest ₹10,000 crore, approximately US$1 billion, to establish a 150 MW hyperscale AI factory in Bodh Gaya , Bihar . The company signed a Letter of Intent with the Government of Bihar for this project. This announcement was made during the inauguration of a new ₹400-crore AI and cloud-ready data center in Patna . Bihar's Chief Minister Shri Samrat Choudhary was present at the inauguration. The greenfield facility in Patna, located in the Patliputra Industrial Area, offers an IT load of 12 MW. This capacity can be expanded based on future demand. Advt Sridhar Pinnapureddy, Founder & CEO, CtrlS Datacenters, stated the company is committed to strengthening Bihar’s digital infrastructure . He added that the company aims to build a robust IT ecosystem through its future-ready data centers. Mr. Pinnapureddy appreciated the Government of Bihar for fostering an industry-friendly business climate and providing incentives. CtrlS Datacenters plans to build over 20 Edge data centers across Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities in India in the coming years. The company, which began operations in 2007, currently operates 19 data centers across nine key Indian markets. CtrlS expects to build over 4.4 GW of data center capacity by 2030. The company also plans to explore new overseas markets, with Thailand being its first international foray. bihar_raw_news.title: CtrlS signs Rs 100 billion LoI with Bihar government to set up 150 MW AI hyperscale factory ...
bihar_raw_news.content: CtrlS Datacenters has signed a letter of intent (LoI) with the government of Bihar to invest Rs 100 billion to set up a 150-megawatt (MW) hyperscale AI factory in Bodh Gaya, and formally inaugurated its Rs 4 billion AI and cloud-ready data centre in Patna. The Patna data centre is located in the Patliputra Industrial Area and currently provides an IT load of 12 MW, with scope for future expansion. The facility is designed to support the digital infrastructure needs of enterprises, government institutions, hyperscalers and technology businesses in Bihar and Eastern India. It is built to be natural disaster-proof and energy-efficient, featuring military-grade security. Looking ahead, CtrlS plans to establish over 20 edge data centres across Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities in India, extending reliable digital infrastructure closer to emerging demand hubs. by tele.net by tele.net 14 Oct 2026 10:33 IST Link copied! bihar_raw_news.title: CtrlS to invest Rs 10000 crore in Bihar to strengthen digital infrastructure
bihar_raw_news.content: CtrlS Datacenters Ltd. has unveiled a major investment plan to boost Bihar’s digital infrastructure. The company has signed a Letter of Intent (LOI) with the Government of Bihar to invest Rs 10,000 crore to set up a 150 MW hyperscale AI factory in Bodh Gaya, in addition to inaugurating its datacenter in Patna. The company’s Rs 400-crore AI and cloud-ready datacenter in Patna was formally inaugurated in the presence of Hon’ble Chief Minister of Bihar, Shri Samrat Choudhary. The datacenter currently offers an IT load of 12 MW with the potential to expand as per future demand. Located in the Patliputra Industrial Area, Patna, the company’s datacenter facility will support the growing digital infrastructure needs of enterprises, government institutions, hyperscalers and technology businesses in Bihar and Eastern India. The greenfield natural disaster-proof, military-grade security, and energy-efficient datacenter expands CtrlS Datacenters’ footprint in the region, further strengthening Bihar’s digital infrastructure landscape and reinforcing its commitment to supporting the growth of Eastern India’s evolving datacenter ecosystem. Sridhar Pinnapureddy, Founder & CEO of CtrlS Datacenters, said, “We are committed to strengthening Bihar’s digital infrastructure and building a robust IT ecosystem through our future-ready datacenters, designed to serve the evolving needs of hyperscalers, enterprises, and startups. We sincerely appreciate the Government of Bihar for creating a conducive policy environment, fostering an industry-friendly business climate, and providing attractive incentives that have supported our investment in the State.” Pinnapureddy added, “Together with our ecosystem partners, we are bringing significant investments into Bihar while creating new employment opportunities and contributing to the region’s economic growth. The strong market potential and growing demand for digital infrastructure have reinforced our confidence in Bihar. In response to this opportunity, CtrlS Datacenters has established this greenfield datacenter in Patna, further strengthening the State’s digital infrastructure ecosystem.” Looking ahead, CtrlS Datacenters is focused on building a hyper-connected network of datacenters across India and beyond, extending reliable digital infrastructure closer to emerging demand hubs. As part of this strategy, the company plans to establish 20+ Edge datacenters across Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities in India over the coming years. As demand grows for localized, low-latency and resilient digital infrastructure, CtrlS is well positioned to accelerate the adoption of Edge datacenters. With a clear roadmap for expansion, the company aims to bring compute and connectivity closer to customers, enabling the next wave of digital services and AI-led applications across India. bihar_raw_news.title: Tokyo promotes sustainable recycling through innovation - ANI News
bihar_raw_news.content: Tokyo promotes sustainable recycling through innovation Updated: 16 hours, 4 min ago Tokyo (Japan), Oct 13 (ANI): “Tokyo Mine” is an initiative to collect used small household appliances containing lithium-ion batteries and for recycling, with the cooperation of Tokyo residents. An AI-powered recycling bin called Bin-e was installed in the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building, and many residents brought lithium-ion batteries from their homes, recovering valuable resources from what is known as an urban mine. Over the past five days, around 50 mobile phones were collected, including other items, total number of collected items rose to more than 10,000. They are transported to a recycling facility, where they are properly processed and recycled. “Tokyo Mine” campaign has ended, but Tokyo Metropolitan Government aims to take leading role in advancing the circular economy. This approach is expected to spread from Tokyo to cities across Asia. bihar_raw_news.title: US AI data center startups raise $33.5 billion in 2026 - ET Datacenters
bihar_raw_news.content: AI & Compute Infrastructure 2 min Read US AI data center startups raise $33.5 billion in 2026 US startups focused on AI data centers secured $33.5 billion in funding by early October 2026, nearly doubling the 2025 total. This investment surge addresses power and computing constraints, driving interest in integrated energy solutions. ETDatacenters Published On Oct 14, 2026 at 07:41 AM IST Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment Highlights US AI data center startups raised $33.5 billion by October 2026. Funding nearly doubled 2025 figures, addressing power and computing constraints. Over 80 per cent of 2026 funds target power supply and computing efficiency. Investment shifts towards integrated power and computing infrastructure solutions. US startups developing technologies for artificial intelligence (AI) data centers raised $33.5 billion in funding by early October 2026, according to a Morgan Stanley report. This figure nearly doubles the total funding raised in 2025. Investors are increasingly supporting technologies that combine energy supply with computing infrastructure, as power availability emerges as a significant challenge for expanding AI data centers . The report highlights that venture funding for this sector accelerated sharply in 2026. The next phase of AI infrastructure development is shifting beyond mere access to computing capacity. It is moving towards integrated systems that coordinate power, computing, networking, and cooling. Power is identified as a key constraint, underscoring the importance of technologies that improve efficiency and secure reliable electricity for data centers. Startups covered in the report have raised over $50 billion since early 2024. This funding spans four areas: expanding power supply, improving computing performance per unit of electricity, integrating power and computing systems, and developing new data center designs and locations. More than 80 per cent of the 2026 funding went to companies focused on expanding power availability and enhancing computing performance relative to electricity consumption. Investment is also broadening from computing technologies into energy infrastructure. In 2026, 73 per cent of funding rounds in the power and computing segments included investors who had previously backed companies in the other segment. This compares to 49 per cent in 2024 and 16 per cent before 2021. The report notes that investors are funding technologies at various development stages. These range from cloud providers deploying computing capacity to advanced nuclear and fusion projects. Companies developing orbital and modular data centers , including Starcloud, Cowboy Space, and Armada, collectively raised nearly $1 billion in 2026. However, the report cautioned that raising capital alone would not be sufficient for commercial viability. It stated that validation should shift from capital raised to capacity deployed. Commercial agreements, regulatory approvals, initial deployments, and evidence of competitive operating costs would become more crucial. The report also pointed out risks from licensing requirements, construction delays, grid connections, and long procurement cycles. bihar_raw_news.content: Adyar-Lighthouse corridor among five projects included in feasibility study Photo | Express Tamil Nadu Rs 98 lakh allotted to prepare DPR for 5 key infra projects State Highways officials said the elevated corridor may run from Pattinapakkam via Loop Road to the Adyar landing near Malar Hospital. B Anbuselvan Updated: 14th Oct, 2026 at 7:24 AM CHENNAI: The state highways has issued a G.O. allocating Rs 98 lakh to prepare detailed project reports (DPRs) for five infrastructure projects in Chennai, including an elevated corridor from the Lighthouse to Adyar near Malar Hospital. The other projects include extending one arm of the Vyasarpadi road overbridge (ROB) towards Madhavaram, widening the ROB at Basin Bridge to ease traffic congestion in North Chennai, widening the bridge across the Cooum river at Koyambedu on the Thirumangalam-Koyambedu stretch of Jawaharlal Nehru Road (Inner Ring Road), and constructing a link road between Rajiv Gandhi Salai and East Coast Road. While four projects were allocated Rs 20 lakh each, one was given Rs 18 lakh, revealed the recent G.O. issued by the department. Official sources in the state highways said the elevated corridor is likely to start from Pattinapakkam, via the Loop Road, and connect to the Adyar landing near Malar Hospital. “The plan is to decongest Santhome High Road, which witnesses heavy traffic during peak hours. Other design parameters, including the length and width of the corridor, will be finalised during the preparation of the DPR,” an official said. Add as a preferred source on Google The department plans to extend one arm of the 1,720-metre-long Y-shaped Vyasarpadi ROB towards Madhavaram. The bridge, which begins near Basin Bridge, branches into two arms - one connecting Moolakadai, Madhavaram and Puzhal and the other leading to Sathyamurthy Nagar Main Road near Kalyanapuram, catering to local traffic. The narrow ROB at Basin Bridge junction, an important link connecting Korukkupet, Vyasarpadi and Purasawalkam, is also set to be widened. The department has also proposed widening the existing six-lane bridge across the Cooum river at Koyambedu, which witnesses heavy congestion during peak hours. A link road connecting Rajiv Gandhi Salai and ECR is proposed, with its alignment and location to be identified during the preparation of the DPR. national_raw_news.content: The First BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ Meeting concluded in New Delhi with the adoption of the Delhi Declaration. In the declaration, the BIMSTEC Nations have strongly condemned terrorism and violent extremism in all its forms and manifestations, including cross-border terrorism. In the declaration, the BIMSTEC nations reiterated their determination to prevent, combat and eliminate terrorism and violent extremism conducive to terrorism in a comprehensive and sustained manner, in accordance with the UN Charter and international law. They also reaffirmed commitment to strengthening regional cooperation under BIMSTEC for realizing a connected, secure, resilient, developed and prosperous BIMSTEC region. They also expressed deepest condolences and solidarity with the victims of terrorist attacks in Member States and their families and with the Governments of the affected States. The nations called for those responsible to be brought to justice in accordance with applicable domestic and international law. The Delhi Declaration also called for effective implementation of the finalized Plans of Action in areas of Human Trafficking, Narcotic Drugs and Precursor Chemicals and Anti-Money Laundering, as well as finalisation of the Plan of Action by the Sub-Group on Cooperation in Countering Radicalization and Terrorism. It also called for effective implementation of the BIMSTEC Convention on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters, which was signed in March 2022 at the 5th BIMSTEC Summit in Colombo. The BIMSTEC nations also reaffirmed the principle that cooperation within BIMSTEC in the security sector is based on respect for the principle of sovereign equality, territorial integrity, political independence, non-interference in internal affairs, non-aggression, peaceful co-existence and mutual respect.

national_raw_news.title: 5 mins ago | National 68 EAM S Jaishankar says India-US trade talks heading in right direction
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has said that India-US trade talks are heading in the right direction and a deal is being ironed out currently. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, Dr Jaishankar informed that trade ministers of the two countries are working on it and both nations are pretty far advanced in the process of negotiations for the trade deal. Replying to a query, Dr Jaishankar emphasised that the US has repositioned itself and every country has to recalibrate and reset its relationship with the US. He highlighted that India has a strong Strategic Partnership with the US. In China, the External Affairs Minister maintained that the bilateral relationship will have consequences if peace and tranquillity in border areas are disturbed. He stated that the relationship is moving towards normalcy as the border areas are settling down. He noted that India and China have been able to restore peace and tranquillity in border areas. Dr Jaishankar remarked that the trade balance between India and China is completely tilted and is extremely one-sided. He said India is not getting a level playing field in China. Replying to another query on Russia, Dr Jaishankar clearly pointed out that India has never encountered a whiff of a suggestion that anything India is procuring from Russia comes with Chinese tech. He opined that because of the Ukraine war, Russia has turned much more to Asia. He said that it is in India’s interest, and the world’s interest, that Russia has multiple choices. He said India is a natural option in that regard.

national_raw_news.title: 8 mins ago | International 8 US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to visit India next week to strengthen energy cooperation &...
national_raw_news.content: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will visit India next week to strengthen energy cooperation and strategic partnership between the two countries. US State Department said, Mr Rubio will travel to Mumbai and Jamnagar during his tour. State Department said, he will meet with senior government officials to strengthen India-US strategic partnership, exchange views on regional and global dynamics, and discuss prospects for enhanced energy cooperation. Mr Rubio will also meet business leaders to promote investment and economic cooperation. This will be Mr Rubio’s second visit to India since May, when he attended the Quad Foreign Ministers’ meeting hosted by External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in New Delhi. Before arriving in India, Mr Rubio will participate in the C5+1 Ministerial meeting in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. The meeting will focus on how strategic cooperation through the diplomatic platform can promote a more peaceful and prosperous future for the US and Central Asian countries. Mr Rubio will also hold bilateral meetings with senior officials from the five Central Asian countries – Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and the Kyrgyz Republic. A US commercial delegation comprising more than 200 business leaders will accompany Mr Rubio to promote stronger commercial cooperation between the US and Central Asia.

national_raw_news.content: Indian Railways Exports 18 Advanced LHB Coaches to Bangladesh Under European Investment Bank Contract News Brief Indian Railways Exports 18 Advanced LHB Coaches To Bangladesh Under European Investment Bank Contract Arjun Brij Oct 14, 2026 | Updated 11:23 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer RCF Kapurthala rolls out LHB coaches for Bangladesh (Pic Via PIB) Indian Railways has dispatched the first batch of 18 broad-gauge passenger coaches to Bangladesh Railway, marking the initial delivery under a Rs 915 crore contract for 200 coaches. The consignment left the Rail Coach Factory in Kapurthala, Punjab, on 12 October and comprises 11 non-air-conditioned Shovan chair cars, three air-conditioned chair cars, two air-conditioned sleeper coaches and two air-conditioned power cars equipped with guard rooms and luggage accommodation. The coaches, manufactured under a European Investment Bank-funded project, feature specially designed reclining seats with stainless steel armrests and footrests, integrated CCTV surveillance systems, passenger alarm systems, and dedicated baby care and prayer rooms. RITES Ltd, the Navratna public sector enterprise handling the export, has previously supplied over 280 locomotives and more than 1,085 coaches globally to countries across Asia, Africa and Latin America. Rail Coach Factory engineers have introduced several technical modifications to meet Bangladesh Railway's specific operational requirements. The electrical system has been reconfigured to operate on a 415-volt system, compared with the standard 750-volt system used on Indian Railways. Additionally, the coach roofs have been structurally reinforced to support the additional weight of passengers travelling on top during peak periods. This export extends a manufacturing partnership that began in 2015-16, when the Kapurthala factory delivered 120 LHB broad-gauge passenger coaches to Bangladesh. Bangladesh Railway placed the fresh order through RITES in 2024, covering seven different variants designed to enhance passenger comfort and safety whilst meeting European Standard EN 15227 collision-safety requirements. The remaining 182 coaches under the 200-coach agreement are scheduled for completion by December 2027. The successful logistics operation has already generated Rs 91.73 lakh in revenue for the Firozpur Railway Division, which managed the coaches' journey from Hussainpur railway station to Darshana railway station in Bangladesh. Daily Excelsior 04:12 AM Oct 14, 2026 IST MLA Reasi Kuldeep Raj Dubey with Neha Jalali (Director, CBC and PIB Jammu) and others at a multimedia exhibition on “12 Years of Government” at Katra. Excelsior Correspondent KATRA, Oct 13: MLA Reasi Kuldeep Raj Dubey today said that India has achieved unprecedented progress across sectors under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, opening new opportunities for youth to contribute towards the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047. He was speaking on the second day of an eight-day multimedia exhibition on “12 Years of Government”, organized by the Central Bureau of Communication (CBC), Jammu, Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, at Katra Advertisement Highlighting transformative initiatives, Dubey said programmes like Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat were strengthening the economy and safeguarding the country's strategic interests. He cited indigenous vaccine development during COVID-19, advancements in defence technology, including S-400 and BrahMos missile systems, and the Chenab Rail Arch Bridge in Reasi as examples of India's technological capabilities. He also highlighted anti-drug initiatives under Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan, including measures undertaken by the Reasi administration during the 100-day campaign, and encouraged youth to explore self-employment opportunities through Central Government startup schemes. Earlier, Neha Jalali, Director, CBC and PIB Jammu, stressed the importance of grassroots awareness and digital media in communicating government initiatives. She urged students and Gen Z to use social platforms constructively to spread awareness about welfare schemes and contribute to positive social change. During the technical sessions, Rakesh Sharma from the Agriculture Department highlighted mushroom cultivation, apiculture and farmer-oriented schemes. Dr Shakti from Community Health Centre (CHC), Katra, discussed maternal and child healthcare, immunization, Ayushman Bharat coverage and the need to prevent drug addiction. Dr Jyoti Jolly from the State TB Office, Jammu, highlighted early TB detection, free treatment under the National TB Elimination Programme and nutritional assistance through Ni-Kshay Poshan Yojana. Abhay Sharma from the Rural Development Department outlined village-level initiatives concerning liquid waste management, rainwater harvesting and composite pits. Locals, tourists and students from Government Higher Secondary School (GHSS), Katra, and GHSS Agar Jitto participated in the programme.
